# Artifact Keeper 1.11.7

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 7 changelog entries from 7 pull requests since 1.11.6, all backported from `main` in #4938 and #4947. The headline is **a retried OCI blob completion no longer fails with 409 "upload session is already being modified"** (#4902, in #4919), which broke `docker push` of large layers through a reverse proxy with a short response timeout, such as Envoy Gateway at its 15 s default. The backend now finishes a completion even when the proxy drops the request, and a same-digest retry gets the same answer. The real fix is still a longer proxy timeout on the `/v2/` routes: see [Reverse proxy timeouts for OCI and Docker pushes](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.7/docs/operations/oci-reverse-proxy-timeouts.md) for the settings for Envoy Gateway, nginx and ingress-nginx. Next to it are replication fixes for protobuf labels, protobuf commits and late format metadata, a Maven concurrent-upload race, the peer network-profile route, a rollback guide warning, and a `crypto-bigint` bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0387. **No schema migrations** (the line stays at migration 289), one new optional setting, and no security advisories ship with this release. Upgrading is a normal image bump.

## What changed

- **A retried OCI blob completion no longer fails with 409 "upload session is already being modified"** (#4902, in #4919). When a reverse proxy timed out the final `PUT ?digest=` of a large layer or the client dropped the connection, the backend abandoned the completion mid-way and left the upload session locked for six hours, so the identical `PUT` that containerd 2.x re-sends after a 504 was refused and the push failed. The completion now runs to its end even when its request is dropped. A retry with the same digest waits for it (up to `OCI_UPLOAD_COMPLETION_RETRY_WAIT_SECS`, default 30 s) and gets the same result, or `503` with `Retry-After` while it is still running; a retry after it finished gets `201`; a retry with a different digest is still `409`. A session held by a replica that died is reclaimable after five minutes instead of six hours. Set the proxy timeouts in [docs/operations/oci-reverse-proxy-timeouts.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.7/docs/operations/oci-reverse-proxy-timeouts.md) so the retry is not needed in the first place.
- **Protobuf commits now replicate to push peers** (#4921, in #4934). A protobuf (BSR) commit row recorded the commit digest as its `checksum_sha256`, so the receiving peer refused every commit push with 409 "checksum mismatch". New commit rows record the sha256 of the stored bundle, and the sync worker corrects older rows before pushing them, with no operator step. A push the peer refuses for one artifact (a checksum mismatch, or an immutable path already occupied) now fails only that task instead of putting the whole peer into retry backoff.
- **Label moves and late format metadata now reach push peers** (#4889, in #4899). The protobuf `_labels` index is now stored as a real JSON object and queued like any other upload, and the NuGet, PyPI, Debian and nested-layout RPM routes queue their push after their format metadata is committed, so a peer no longer receives an artifact without it. Client-uploaded `maven-metadata.xml` stays unpushed by design: peers regenerate it from the versioned artifacts they receive.
- **Concurrent first Maven uploads of one release coordinate can no longer leave the winner's row pointing at the loser's bytes** (#4892, in #4897). The object is now written inside the publishing transaction under the per-key publish lock, and an upload that finds the coordinate already published returns `409` without touching the winner's storage key. In Artifactory migration path mode a hosted Maven upload also writes its object once instead of twice (#4893).
- **`PUT /api/v1/peers/{id}/network-profile` now reaches its handler** (#4884, in #4906). The route had been mounted without the `:id` segment and answered with a 500 carrying a raw extractor error. It now requires the peer ID, rejects a malformed ID with `400` and answers `404` for an unknown peer.
- **The rollback guide warns that a 1.11.x database cannot serve a 1.10.x backend for OCI pushes** (#4915, in #4917). Migration 243 (1.11.0) replaced a unique key the 1.10.x upload path relies on, so after a rollback to 1.10.x every `docker push` failed. [docs/operations/rollback.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.7/docs/operations/rollback.md) now says so up front and lists the releases that cannot be rolled back across.

### Security

- **`crypto-bigint` bumped 0.7.5 to 0.7.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0387** (#4941). `crypto-bigint` 0.7.5 could take secret-dependent branches in some operations intended to be constant-time. It reaches the backend through the `bergshamra` XML signature crates. Lockfile-only, with no behaviour change. A second copy, 0.5.5, remains through `elliptic-curve` 0.13 because the 0.5 line has no patched release; the advisory carries a documented exception in `.cargo/audit.toml` until the dependent crates move off it, tracked in #4940.

## Upgrade notes

A normal image bump. There is no migration and no change to any existing setting. Two things operators of OCI and Docker repositories may notice:

- An upload session left behind by a completion whose replica died is now reclaimable after **five minutes** instead of six hours, so a client retry after a crash or pod kill succeeds much sooner.
- New optional variable **`OCI_UPLOAD_COMPLETION_RETRY_WAIT_SECS`** (default `30`, `0` answers at once, capped at 3600) sets how long a retried completion `PUT` waits for the completion it duplicates before answering `503` with `Retry-After`. The default suits most deployments; raising your proxy's `/v2/` response timeout is the better fix for slow completions.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.7]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.7/CHANGELOG.md).
